newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia bows to rebels, orders troop pull-out.
newsitem.headline: Colombia bows to rebels, orders troop pull-out.

text.p: President Ernesto Samper granted sweeping concessions on Tuesday to Colombia's largest guerrilla army in a bid to persuade it to free 60 soldiers it captured almost nine months ago.

After two days of meetings with military commanders, Samper pledged to withdraw security forces from a 5,000 square mile (13,000 sq km) area of jungle in southern Caqueta province for 32 days starting at midnight on Thursday.

The Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), set up as a pro-Soviet force in 1964, seized the troops when it overran the Las Delicias military base in neighbouring Putumayo province on Aug. 30 last year. At least 27 soldiers died in the attack which heralded the start of one of the bloodiest rebel offensives in more than three decades of guerrilla uprising.

"I hope this decision is seen by the armed (guerrilla) groups as a gesture in favour of peace, defence of human rights and reconciliation that all Colombian people are calling for," Samper said in a speech at the presidential palace.

The 32-day demilitarization is almost double the time FARC commanders had been calling for. Samper also bowed to rebel chieftains' demands that the town of Remolinos del Caguan, site of a military garrison, be included in the demilitarized zone.

Army chiefs had previously refused to pull out of Remolinos, arguing that it was a key point on rebel-managed cocaine smuggling routes. Since the army arrived the town's population has dwindled to less than 100 from about 5,000.

In comments to Reuters over the weekend one, of the FARC's international spokesmen said the rebel group would release in a single group all 60 soldiers, together with 10 marines captured in fighting in northwest Choco province in January.

FARC representatives were not immediately available to comment on Samper's decision on Tuesday, which if successful would end Latin America's longest-running hostage saga -- largely overshadowed by the recent siege of the Japanese embassy residence in Lima.
